reads.title: Why one move, and Hill next week
reads.body:
You made two transfers in GW11, Verbruggen for Suzuki and Konsa for Vuskovic, so Calafiori and Szoboszlai are still here and you have one free transfer. Their problem is still minutes: the model expects about 74 a game from Calafiori and 59 from Szoboszlai.

Tavernier is the clear first move. He projects 32.5 points over GW12 to GW17 against 17.9 for Szoboszlai, and the swap alone adds a projected 9.2 against making no transfers. He is in 70% of teams near your rank, so this also closes a template gap. He joins Silva at Bournemouth; Hill next week would make three, the most the rules allow.

The model's best plan also sells Calafiori for Hill, at a 4 point hit, for a projected 11.7. That is 2.5 ahead of the free plan and clears both of our hit bars: 2 points over the horizon and 6 over four gameweeks (7.8). But that comparison assumes Calafiori is never sold. You can sell him next week with the GW13 free transfer instead, four days later, and give up only Hill's 1.3 point lead in GW12. The hit would free next week's transfer for something else, and the best such move, Raya for Trafford, projects 3.4. Put together, the hit is worth about 0.7 over waiting, which is inside the model's error, while the 4 points are certain. So the edition overrides the model here and skips the hit.

The plan for GW13, a projection to recheck with next week's data: Calafiori out, Hill in, projected +6.7 over GW13 to GW18.

reads.title: How last week went
reads.body:
These are facts from your FPL history and the prediction log, scored after GW11 was final.

You scored 33, two below the average of 35, and your rank fell from 82,568 to 110,661. The week was lost on the bench and the armband. Calvert-Lewin and Szoboszlai scored 9 each and Suzuki 6, all on the bench, while Raya started and scored 1. De Cuyper captained for 1, so 2 in all.

The edition's call did not do better. Gabriel for Calafiori was 1 for 1, and Tavernier for Szoboszlai was 8 for 9, so the two moves netted -1 against a projected +4.4 for that week. Captain Haaland scored 2. The call's eleven with Haaland captain would have scored 41, eight more than you did.

The Free Hit would have scored 59 against 39 for the call's eleven, 20 more, against a projected gain of 2.4. One week like that does not change the plan, but it is a reminder that the model's projected gaps are small next to real swings.

The model missed by 2.0 points a player on average across 374 players and was too low by 0.3 on balance. It gave hauls of 10 or more a 1.4% chance on average; 4.6% of players hauled, the known bias toward flat projections.

reads.title: Why the Free Hit still waits
reads.body:
Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline, 1 Jan 18:30 UK. Every gameweek before then has all ten fixtures, so the chip is about fixtures and rotation, not rescuing a blank.

The planner projects Free Hit gains of 4.1 to 8.8 points a week from GW12 to GW19. GW19 is now the tallest bar at 8.8, GW14 is at 8.0 and GW18 at 7.3. This week projects 5.3. The festive run puts three deadlines in seven days (26 Dec, 29 Dec and 1 Jan), when rotation is hardest to call, so GW18 and GW19 remain the window. GW19 now leads GW18 by 1.5, but these weeks are four to six gameweeks out and the model has no rotation model, so the decision stays on 26 Dec, with real team news.

data_room.title: The hit, weighed in full
data_room.body:
## Method

The planner scores a squad by the best eleven it can field each week from GW12 to GW17, with the captain counted twice, bench points at 10% and each later week weighted 8% less. A plan's gain is that score minus the score of making no transfers, minus 4 for each transfer beyond your one free one. It searched every one and two transfer plan against the best projected players in each position, then extended the strongest with a third. Only legal squads count: three per club, within your £1.2m bank and your selling prices.

## The numbers

| Plan | Gain, 6 GWs | Hit | Bank after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai → Hill, Tavernier | +11.7 | -4 | £1.1m |
| Calafiori, Szoboszlai, Raya → Hill, Tavernier, Trafford | +11.5 | -8 | £2.1m |
| Calafiori, Palmer → Hill, Tavernier | +10.4 | -4 | £4.1m |
| Szoboszlai → Tavernier (the call) | +9.2 | 0 | £1.1m |
| Roll | 0 | 0 | £1.2m |

Gains are after any hit. Every plan in the top twelve but the call pays at least 4.

## Why the model's plan is not the call

Our rule takes a -4 only when it beats the best free plan by 2 or more over the horizon and clears 6 over four gameweeks. The model's plan passes both: +2.5 over six gameweeks, and +7.8 over GW12 to GW15 after the hit.

The rule compares the hit with a free plan that keeps Calafiori for all six weeks. The real choice is between selling him now for 4 points and selling him in GW13 with the free transfer you get anyway. The second path gives up Hill's GW12 lead over Calafiori, 4.9 against 3.6, so about 1.3. The hit path keeps GW13's free transfer for another move; from the squad after the hit, the best one is Raya for Trafford, +3.4 over GW13 to GW18, and that leans on Raya's shoulder (50% chance of playing) and is a bench keeper. Net: -4 + 1.3 + 3.4 is about +0.7 for the hit. The hit rule should be extended to compare against the next week's free path; that is a change for the backtest to test, not for this week.

Hill for Calafiori next week, from the squad after the call, projects +6.7 over GW13 to GW18 and fits the bank (Hill £5.7m, Calafiori sells for £5.7m).

## How confident we are

Fairly confident in Tavernier: most of his gain is Szoboszlai's 59 expected minutes against his 88, and he is in 70% of teams near your rank. Less confident in Hill. Minutes are the model's weakest input, and it leans toward defenders who earn defensive contribution points, which is part of why Hill projects 9 points above Calafiori. Last week the Calafiori sale (for Gabriel) scored 1 for 1. The model cannot see transfers made since the GW11 deadline, so check your squad before you confirm.

data_room.title: When to play your first Free Hit
data_room.intro: Your first Free Hit expires at the GW19 deadline (1 Jan, 18:30 UK). There are no blank gameweeks before then, so its value comes from fixtures and rotation.
data_room.bottom_line: Still GW18 or GW19. Decide on 26 Dec, with real team news.
data_room.body:
## What moved this week

GW19 is now the tallest bar at 8.8, ahead of GW14 at 8.0 and GW18 at 7.3. A week ago GW14 led at 7.8 with GW18 and GW19 just behind. Projections this far out move week to week, which is why the decision waits.

## Why GW18 first, still

GW19 projects 1.5 more than GW18. That is a real gap on paper, but it is four to six gameweeks out and the v0 model has no rotation model, which is exactly what the festive run tests. GW18 comes after the Boxing Day games, so you see who was rested, and it keeps GW19 as a fallback. Waiting for GW19 leaves no second chance before the chip expires. If GW19 still leads by more than a point on 26 Dec, play it there.

## Last week, as a check

In GW11 the Free Hit eleven would have scored 59 against 39 for the call's eleven, 20 more, against a projected gain of 2.4. One week, but it shows how much a single week's swing can exceed the projected gap.

## How this was worked out

For each gameweek, the planner builds the best eleven your £101.6m budget allows, keeping money back for a cheap bench, and compares it with the best eleven from your current squad. The captain counts double in both. Projections come from the v0 model.
data_room.confidence: Not very, and that is why the call is to wait. Treat any gap under 1 point as a tie. Play it early only if three or more starters are out in the same week.
